clesRetenues: Q Richard Vosser (JPMorgan) - does H1 support confidence in the 9-12% long-term BPS target: management cites the double-digit growth trajectory of consumables, solid commercial drug demand, a healthy approval pipeline and improving biotech funding.
Q Charles Weston (RBC) - did Q2 operating growth include the tailwind from tariff surcharges, and how large: yes, +40bp in Q2, treated as an operating fact.

Q Charles Weston (RBC) - detail on the delayed programmes, scale of the headwind, confidence on orders returning: two key clients have delayed late-stage advanced-therapy projects for timing reasons, orders expected at year-end, revenue likely in 2027.

Q Subbu Nambi (Guggenheim) - are the advanced-modality delays linked to the monoclonal antibody issues flagged by peers: no link, delays isolated to two advanced-therapy clients, unrelated to the protein portfolio.

Q Subbu Nambi (Guggenheim) - why assume the delays are temporary rather than permanent: client discussions point to a timing shift rather than programme cancellations, resolution expected at year-end/early 2027.

Q James Quigley (Goldman Sachs) - which metrics demonstrate strong underlying BPS consumables demand supporting continued double-digit growth: large CDMO/biopharma clients show broad-based growth in late-stage/commercial production, classical and advanced therapies alike, providing visibility.

Q Odysseas Manesiotis (BNP Paribas) - which equipment/consumables product groups drove the persistent mix headwind: not a recurring vs non-recurring mix issue, but delays in higher-margin ATS products creating negative mix effects within the categories.

Q Charlie Haywood (BofA) - quantify chromatography/purification exposure as a % of BPS, and whether client delays are broadening beyond those mentioned: no percentage provided, client delays isolated with no visible trend across products or clients.

Q Falko Friedrich (Deutsche Bank) - should H2 be modelled with balanced Q3/Q4 growth or are there specific phasing effects: no quarterly guidance provided, the main technical factors being the MatTek exit and the tariff effect reversing from tailwind to headwind in H2.

Q Oliver Reinberg (Kepler Cheuvreux) - with favourable 2027 comps, why not target the high end of the 9-12% medium-term range: will be addressed at the appropriate time, current tariff uncertainties preventing speculation beyond the current guidance.

Q Harry Sephton (Berenberg) - why does the midpoint of the BPS range imply a deceleration despite the Q1-Q2 acceleration and improving end markets: the H1 tariff tailwind reverses into a headwind in H2, with no net growth impulse for the year at current rates.

Q Charles Pitman-King (Barclays) - since when has the potential tariff refund become a strategy, and does the transparency differentiate Sartorius from peers: refunds unexpected, claim filed as peers did but payment received only at end-June, client compensation reflecting a partnership philosophy.

Q James Vane-Tempest (Jefferies) - explain the APAC acceleration and the stocking patterns, and the gross margin benefit from prior-year inventory write-downs: APAC momentum driven by the China recovery in consumables, stocking minimal and scattered, inventory benefits fading gradually over several quarters.

Q Oliver Metzger (ODDO BHF) - confirm the equipment growth expectations for H2, and when convergence towards the consumables level: equipment expected flat to modest growth, convergence dependent on client capacity additions, management awaiting more visibility on orders.

Q Thibault Boutherin (Morgan Stanley) - Americas bioprocessing performance excluding tariff/ATS effects, and orders tied to onshoring: excluding tariff and ATS effects, North America shows healthy growth, onshoring projects materialising as brownfield, majority of orders expected in H2 2027, sales impact 2028+.
Q Charles Weston (RBC, follow-up) - has the 10 M€ Iran sanctions risk estimate for 2026 changed: no change, the 10 M€ estimate remains valid.

dernierCall.guidanceProchainTrimestre: No quarterly guidance given. H2 phasing flagged: MatTek contribution rolls off from July; tariff surcharges flip from H1 tailwind (+40bp in Q2) to H2 headwind (no net FY growth impulse if tariffs stay at 10%); FX turns into a tailwind of slightly below 50bp in each of Q3 and Q4; equipment revenue in absolute terms expected higher in H2 than H1.
dernierCall.guidanceAnnuelle: FY26 confirmed for SSB: sales +6-10% cc. Newly introduced 'operational' view (excluding the ~EUR 35m customer tariff compensation, tariff assumptions frozen as of July 24, 2026): broadly around the midpoint (~8% cc); including the compensation effect, cc growth expected in the lower half of the range. Underlying EBITDA margin slightly above 31% (H1 ran at 31.4%); CapEx ratio around the prior-year level of slightly above 13% of sales; net debt/underlying EBITDA slightly above 2x at year-end (2.36x at H1); FX headwind ~2pts on FY reported revenue growth. Group frame also confirmed: +5-9% cc, margin slightly above 30%; BPS +6-10%, margin slightly above 32%; LPS +2-6%, margin slightly below 21%.
pointsCles: Core thesis catalyst firming up: the equipment business - muted since 2022 - stabilized and returned to slight organic growth in H1 26 ('the bottom is behind us'), while consumables grew >9% operationally (double-digit CAGR since 2019, volumes now above the pandemic peak); Faber reiterated the 9-12% mid-term BPS growth ambition and sees FY26 recurring revenue in the high-single to low-double-digit range.

US tariff technicality dominates the optics: after the Feb-2026 Supreme Court ruling voided IEEPA tariffs, SSB received EUR 22m of EUR 35m refunds claimed (~13m outstanding, timing uncertain) and books an equivalent customer-compensation liability that cuts reported revenue - a 1.5pt cc growth drag in H1 (~3pt in Q2); surcharges added +40bp in Q2 and flip to a headwind in H2 (net ~zero over the full year at the current 10% tariff level), with negligible margin impact - underlying economics unchanged.

Advanced-therapy order delays at two large late-stage customers: management insists on project timing, not cancellations, and explicitly denies any link to Danaher's mAb customer delays; orders expected late 2026/early 2027 with revenue mostly landing in 2027; ex-ATS the recurring business would be double-digit, and the delayed high-margin ATS consumables also explain the adverse product-mix effect within the margin bridge.

Below the line and balance sheet: underlying net profit EUR 235m (+3%, EPS 2.42), reported net profit EUR 181m (+17.6%); operating cash flow +39% to EUR 341m, FCF nearly doubled to EUR 199m; leverage improved to 2.36x (vs 2.38x YE25) despite the CellGenix minority buyout (EUR 72m, SSB now at 100%) and the dividend; May bond refinancing oversubscribed; regions: APAC +12.5% cc led (China recovery), EMEA +7.7%, Americas +5.4% operational cc (+0.8% incl. tariff compensation); brand fee to Sartorius AG up 25bp since Q1 26 after German tax audits.

hypothese.summary: Bioprocessing pure-player, 71,5%-owned subsidiary of Sartorius AG. THESIS VALIDATED in H1 26: equipment has stabilised and is back to growth as expected, consumables remain >9% organic. New CMD March 2026 targets (revenue +9-12%/yr, margin +60-85bp/yr from 2027) refine and confirm the trajectory. One caveat only: slower deleveraging than expected (CellGenix + dividend consumed H1 FCF) and a technical tariff effect that temporarily clouds the read on reported revenue.
hypothese.text:
== THESIS SUMMARY ==
Pure-play world bioprocessing supplier, 71.5%-owned by Sartorius AG (83% of votes). The cyclical-recovery thesis posed at creation (07/07/2026) passed its first test: equipment - mute since 2022 - 'stabilized as expected and back to slight growth' in H1, while high-margin recurring consumables keep compounding >9% organic. FY26 guidance confirmed: +6/10% cc (operational ~8% ex-tariff effect), underlying EBITDA margin slightly above 31%.

== THESIS READ ==
- The equipment cycle turning is THE thesis driver - one semester of evidence in, more needed. Watch: equipment order intake each half.
- Consumables >9% organic is the quality floor under the recovery. Watch: destocking fully behind in all regions.
- Deleveraging is the below-the-line kicker: finNet -130M (2025) improving to ~-48M by 2030 (May-2026 refinancing at 3.75% coupon), compounding EPS ahead of EBIT. Watch: refinancing schedule execution.

== SPECIAL FACTORS ==
Base = normalized IFRS: underlying EBITDA minus FULL D&A including ~110M/yr IFRS3 acquisition amortization KEPT (vs management 'underlying' which excludes it) - wedge documented; the amortization figure was re-derived from published S1 actuals (54.7M/6m), refining the ~155M creation estimate (E5bis confrontation done). ETR 26% = management's own interim rate. Shares constant (92M).

== PARAMETERS & WATCH-LIST ==
2026: revenue 3,100M, EBIT 645M (Omnium base), EPS 4.35; 2027-2030: revenue +9.5%/yr, margin expansion per the March-2026 CMD frame, net debt 2,173 -> 350M. Watch: CMD mid-term targets vs delivery; parent-company (Sartorius AG) structural decisions; China bioprocessing demand.

== CATALYSTS ==
Q3 (Oct); equipment order-book inflection confirmation; FY26 (late Jan 2027) with FY27 frame; deleveraging milestones.

ancrages.moteur: Equipment business stabilised as expected and back to slight organic growth in H1 26 (vs near-stagnation 2022-2025), confirmed by consumables >9% organic and the maintained revenue guidance
CMD March 2026: organic revenue growth 9-12%/yr cc from 2027 (100-200bp above the bioprocessing market at 8-10%/yr) - taken at ~9,5% reported (~1pt FX deduction)
CMD March 2026: underlying EBITDA margin expansion of 60-85bp/yr from 2027 (operating leverage, growing share of consumables) - taken at the midpoint of the range ~72,5bp/yr
Guidance confirmed at H1 26: underlying EBITDA margin 'slightly above 31%' - taken at 31,3%, consistent with the 31,4% already reported in H1 26

Tax rate explicitly guided and applied by management for the calculation of the interim results: 26% (identical in 2025 and 2026), rolled forward across the whole projection horizon absent information to the contrary

Reported H1 26 net financial result -57,5 M€ (vs -62,2 M€ in H1 25), an improvement driven by lower interest charges and positive FX/valuation effects. The May 2026 bond refinancing (2023 tranche refinanced through Sartorius Finance B.V. at an explicit 3,75% coupon, priority 1 E5-a-bis) reduces the prospective cost of funding - improving trajectory retained through 2030 as leverage comes down

Net debt of 2 198,7 M€ at 30/06/26 (vs 2 173,1 M€ at end-2025, broadly flat instead of the expected decline), H1 FCF (198,8 M€) having been absorbed by the FY25 dividend (67,9 M€) and the buyout of the CellGenix minorities (71,8 M€). Guidance confirmed: net debt/EBITDA 'slightly above 2x' at end-2026 (vs 2,38x at end-2025), implying deleveraging concentrated in H2. Rebasing of the omniumND trajectory vs the creation refresh (1 850 M€ projected at end-2026, now 2 050 M€)

Exercise of the call option on the remaining 24% minority interest in Sartorius CellGenix GmbH for ~71,8 M€ (SSB now holds 100%) - slightly accretive to net income attributable to the group (removal of the minority share), a minor effect but retained in projected net income

IFRS3/intangibles amortisation tied to the serial acquisitions (Polyplus, CellGenix, BIA Separations) explicitly kept in the Omnium base (E5-e, serial acquirer): ~109-115 M€/yr on the basis of reported H1 26 (54,7 M€ over 6 months) - a more precise figure than the ~155 M€/yr estimate used at creation, recalculated once with explicit confrontation (E5bis)
